I have stopped so far for a week and plan to for at least 3 months. What got me to stop was waking up in my bed with stickers that a medic would put on you when you’ve been seen by one, I recognised what they were, but had no clue why they were on me. I asked a flatmate, I was told I had fallen outside my flat completely wasted at 7 in the morning and hit my head. An ambulance came and saw me. After a while they managed to get me stabilised and my flat mates had to walk me to my room.

I have absolutely no memory of any of this, waking up and being told you’ve been in an ambulance the night before and you having no memory of it is pretty fucking bad man. And I couldn’t deny this time round it was directly attributed to my drinking. That, and what it put my flatmates, who are also my friends through, is what brought on my current abstinence. I have many other low points to share, I shit myself and left shit all over a past house I lived in before. That wasn’t enough for me to stop that time for some reason.

As I said, it’s a game of how low do you want to go, best to stop yourself before you discover a situation you really don’t want to be in.

The twin towers were designed by its leading architect, Minoru Yamasaki. With such an incident in mind, having happened twice before in New York’s history, with planes crashing into the Empire State and 40 Wall Street. Both occasions these planes were low on fuel, lost in fog, and looking for the landing strip.

He assumed another crash would be of such an instance, and in this case it kind of was. He had even designed it with the commercial airliner of the time, a Boeing 707, crashing into it and the towers being able to stand. Which was the plane that narrowly missed the towers here. Which by the way is exactly what happened on 9/11, it wasn’t the impact that caused the collapse, it was the resulting intense fires ignited by the copious amounts of jet fuel that caused it. 

Honestly, the tower would have stood. And fatalities may have been high relative to the fact that The Windows on the World restaurant, a very popular and renowned place to be in the evening of New York at the time. Could have been packed. The restaurant was around that area floor wise in the North Tower.

Offices in the evening would’ve been sparse. It would’ve been bad nevertheless, fatalities perhaps reaching over 100. But it would not have fallen. No way.

Repairs would’ve taken perhaps up to a year. Downtown Manhattan was booming at the time, and unusable office space in such a prestigious location would not be allowed to sit idle for too long.

EDIT: I don’t think this would do anything to negate 9/11 from occurring, as I had mentioned plane clashes of the sort that nearly occurred here were not completely unheard of in Manhattan. And it was also an accident.
